episode.title: Serialize policy persistence and validate stored regular-expression rules
episode.before: At parent be2ebd1772e3562f4caf535067bb2d0e071ae6b8, every persistent policy-update event independently read, modified, and wrote the same auto-saved TOML file. All writes shared one fixed `<policyFile>.tmp` staging path and used a non-exclusive write, so overlapping events could read stale state, lose one another's rules, or race while renaming the same temporary file. Raw `argsPattern` values were also compiled and admitted without length or nested-quantifier safety checks.
episode.after: At 6d3fff2ea445c18348c76feb72f524f2b685be21, one promise queue per policy updater serializes persistent read-modify-write operations. Each operation stages serialized TOML in a random-suffixed temporary file opened exclusively with `wx`, closes its handle, and atomically renames it to the target. A shared regular-expression validator rejects invalid, overlong, and nested-quantifier patterns before dynamic rule admission and while loading persisted policy and safety-checker rules.
episode.diff: The change imports cryptographic randomness and a new regex-safety helper; adds a sequential persistence promise chain; replaces the fixed temporary pathname and direct `writeFile` with a random temporary pathname, exclusive file creation, handle-based writing and closing, then rename; validates raw regex patterns at both update and TOML-load boundaries; and updates tests for exclusive staging plus tests for unsafe-pattern rejection. Six policy implementation/test files changed.

evidence_units.claim: Commit 6d3fff2ea445c18348c76feb72f524f2b685be21 has parent be2ebd1772e3562f4caf535067bb2d0e071ae6b8 and subject `fix(core): prevent race condition in policy persistence (#18506)`.

The parent implementation performed each persistent event's read-modify-write directly, used the shared path `${policyFile}.tmp`, wrote it with `fs.writeFile`, and renamed it to the policy file without a serialization queue.

The updated policy updater creates a promise-based persistence queue and appends each persistent read-modify-write operation to that queue, preventing overlapping operations within one updater instance.

Each queued write now uses an eight-byte random hexadecimal suffix, opens the temporary file with exclusive `wx` semantics, writes through the returned handle, closes it in a finally block, and renames it to the stable policy pathname.
Persistent behavior is entered through the UPDATE_POLICY message subscriber only when the incoming message has `persist` enabled; non-persistent updates still modify only the in-memory policy engine.

Persistence tests publish UPDATE_POLICY messages and assert that the implementation opens a `.tmp` path with `wx`, writes the expected TOML through the file handle, and renames the staging file to `auto-saved.toml`; command-prefix and provider-qualified rule representations remain covered.
The new regex validator first checks compilation, rejects patterns longer than 2048 characters, and heuristically rejects groups containing a quantifier that are themselves quantified.
Dynamic policy updates reject an unsafe raw args pattern before adding an in-memory rule or reaching persistence, while command-prefix patterns continue through the escaped pattern builder.

The TOML loader applies the same safety predicate to persisted policy rules and safety-checker rules, records a regex-compilation error for unsafe patterns, and excludes those entries from the loaded rule sets.
Unit tests accept representative simple, quantified, and grouped patterns and reject malformed, 2049-character, and nested-quantifier patterns.
The policy-updater test publishes an update containing `(a+)+` and verifies that no policy rule is added.
The commit changed the policy updater, persistence tests, updater tests, TOML loader, regex utility, and regex utility tests.

The checked-in tests provide direct oracles for exclusive temporary-file creation, serialized TOML content, atomic rename invocation, regex classification, and rejection at the live update boundary; the commit does not add a test that drives two persistent updates concurrently.

candidate_atomics.name: serialize_persistent_read_modify_write
candidate_atomics.title: Serialize persistent read-modify-write updates
candidate_atomics.description: Route state-changing persistence requests through a per-owner promise chain so each operation observes the result of the preceding operation before reading and appending state.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent concurrent persistence events in one process from losing previously accepted state through overlapping reads and writes.
semantic_action.pre_state: Multiple accepted persistence events can independently enter the same read-parse-append-write sequence against one state file.
semantic_action.post_state: Each persistence operation starts only after the preceding queued operation has completed, so later reads can observe earlier committed updates.
semantic_action.validation: Publish multiple persistent updates without awaiting individual listener completion, then verify the final parsed state contains every rule in queue order and no persistence-error feedback was emitted. The implementation establishes the queue, but this exact concurrent oracle is not present in the changed tests.

candidate_atomics.name: isolate_atomic_write_staging
candidate_atomics.title: Give each atomic write an exclusive staging file
candidate_atomics.description: Create a unique temporary file exclusively, write and close it, then rename it over the stable state file so writers do not contend for one shared staging pathname.

semantic_action.intent: Prevent temporary-file collisions and incomplete replacement during persistent state writes.
semantic_action.pre_state: Writers share one predictable temporary pathname and create or truncate it through a non-exclusive write.
semantic_action.post_state: Each write owns a newly created unique staging file, closes it after complete serialization, and replaces the stable target through rename.
semantic_action.validation: Assert the staging pathname ends in `.tmp`, is opened with `wx`, receives the serialized state through its handle, is closed, and is renamed to the stable target; exercise two writers to verify distinct staging names.

candidate_atomics.name: validate_regex_state_at_ingress
candidate_atomics.title: Reject unsafe regular expressions at every state-ingress boundary
candidate_atomics.description: Apply one bounded regex-safety predicate before admitting live updates and before reconstructing runtime objects from persisted configuration.

semantic_action.intent: Keep invalid or potentially pathological regular expressions out of both active and restored policy state.
semantic_action.pre_state: Raw regex strings from update messages or persisted configuration can be compiled directly into active policy and checker rules.
semantic_action.post_state: Only syntactically valid patterns within the length bound and without the detected nested-quantifier form become active rules; rejected entries produce feedback or loader errors.
semantic_action.validation: Classify accepted and rejected pattern examples, verify an unsafe live update does not add a rule, and verify unsafe persisted policy and checker entries are reported and omitted.

candidate_workflows.name: make_file_backed_policy_updates_race_safe_and_schema_safe
candidate_workflows.title: Make file-backed policy updates race-safe and safe to restore
candidate_workflows.description: A partial-order resolution chain for mutable structured state that is updated asynchronously, atomically replaced on disk, and later reconstructed into executable objects.

workflow_graph.goal: Preserve every accepted policy update in valid TOML while preventing same-process lost updates, staging-file collisions, and restoration of unsafe regex state.
when_to_use: An event-driven component performs read-modify-write updates against one persistent structured-state file.
Concurrent or closely spaced updates can read the same prior snapshot or share a temporary pathname.
Persisted fields are later compiled or interpreted as executable matching expressions.
anti_goals: Do not change policy precedence, decisions, or the representation of accepted rule fields.
Do not serialize unrelated in-memory operations that do not request persistence.
Do not treat the heuristic regex check as a complete regular-expression complexity proof or silently rewrite rejected patterns.
not_applicable_when: The state store already provides a transactional compare-and-swap or equivalent multi-writer update primitive.
Every write replaces a complete authoritative snapshot and lost-update preservation is not required.
Persisted values are inert data and are never compiled or interpreted as matching expressions.
inputs: The persistent update event and its persist flag
The stable state-file location and current serialized contents
The raw expression fields admitted live or restored from disk
workflow_graph.entry_state: Accepted updates may overlap during read-modify-write, writers share a fixed staging pathname, and raw expression fields can enter active or restored state without bounded safety validation.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Each accepted expression satisfies the shared ingress predicate, same-process persistent updates execute sequentially, every write uses an exclusive unique staging file followed by rename, and rejected persisted entries are reported rather than activated.

steps.condition: Apply when an update or persisted record contains a raw regular-expression field; escaped command-prefix-derived patterns remain on their existing trusted construction path.
steps.validation: Unsafe live patterns add no rule; malformed, overlong, and detected nested-quantifier patterns fail the predicate; unsafe restored entries are reported and omitted.

steps.condition: Apply only to accepted events whose persistence flag is enabled.
steps.validation: A concurrent-update test should show that all accepted rules survive in the final parsed file; code inspection confirms each operation is chained from the preceding promise.

steps.condition: Apply for every queued replacement of the stable state file.
steps.validation: Verify exclusive `wx` creation of a unique `.tmp` path, handle-based write and close, then rename to the stable target.

validation_ladder: Unit-test the expression predicate with valid, malformed, overlong, and nested-quantifier examples.
Test the live update boundary to prove a rejected expression cannot mutate active state.
Test serialization content and the exclusive staging-file/open/write/rename protocol.
Add a concurrent persistent-update test that controls read/write timing and proves the final file contains every accepted update.
Load the resulting file and verify all accepted rules reconstruct successfully while unsafe stored rules are reported and omitted.
stop_conditions: Stop if the updater cannot identify one stable state target or cannot scope a serialization owner around all same-process writers.
Stop if expression-bearing inputs cannot be identified before compilation or persistence.
Do not claim multi-process lost-update prevention from unique staging files alone; the queue is local to one updater instance.
Do not claim the race is regression-tested until a test actually overlaps at least two persistence operations.
unresolved_or_deferred: No changed test directly overlaps two persistent UPDATE_POLICY events, so the queue's lost-update guarantee is supported by implementation structure rather than a dedicated regression oracle.
The per-updater promise queue does not coordinate separate processes or separate updater instances writing the same target.
The regex check is explicitly heuristic and is not a complete ReDoS analysis.
The changed tests do not directly exercise unsafe regex rejection in the TOML loader's policy-rule and safety-checker branches.

unresolved_questions: Was cross-process concurrent writing in scope? Unique temporary files prevent staging-name collisions, but no filesystem lock or transactional merge protects two processes that read the same prior target state.

Because the checkout worktree contains broad pre-existing deletions unrelated to this commit, validation was based on pinned Git objects and checked-in tests; tests were not executed against the dirty worktree.
GitHub PR body, review discussion, and status checks are unavailable in the supplied evidence bundle.
